terms.definition: The energy an object has because it is moving.
terms.function: Rises with motion; converted into potential or heat when the object slows.
terms.whereItIs: The energy bar beside the rolling cart.
terms.whyItMatters: Behind every crash, brake, and fast ball, it measures motion's power to do.

terms.definition: The formula kinetic energy = half × mass × speed squared.
terms.whyItMatters: It explains why speed dominates energy and why fast things hit so hard.
terms.whereItIs: Implied by the sliders and the fill bar.

terms.definition: The reason doubling speed produces four times the kinetic energy (2² = 4).
terms.whyItMatters: It is behind braking-distance rules and speed-limit rationale.
terms.whereItIs: The speed slider the bar reacts to.

terms.whyItMatters: Every energy amount — kinetic, potential, electrical — is totaled in joules.
terms.whereItIs: Shown as the unit on the energy bar.
